original_question: Can one construct a flat Hermitian metric H_X on H^0(SU_X(r), L^k) such that the image of the projective monodromy representation ρ_{r,k} is contained in the projective unitary group PU(H_X)?
target_in_paper: Q8 in §9 ('The projective connection'), the open problem stated immediately after Theorem 7 and Q7. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures Beauville's Q8 almost verbatim: it asks for a flat Hermitian metric H_X on H^0(SU_X(r), L^k) and uses the paper's own equivalent reformulation that the image of the projective monodromy representation rho_{r,k} should lie in the projective unitary group PU(H_X). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001))
missing_details: X should be identified as a smooth compact Riemann surface (curve) of genus g; Beauville says he usually assumes g >= 2 from §1 onward. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001))
SU_X(r) should be defined as the moduli space of semistable rank-r vector bundles on X with trivial determinant. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001))
L should be defined as the determinant line bundle on SU_X(r). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001))

The problem is about the projectively flat bundle obtained when X varies in a family of smooth curves; without this, 'flat Hermitian metric' on a single fibre is underspecified. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001))

rho_{r,k} should be defined from Theorem 7 and Q7: for T = M_g (more accurately the moduli stack, as Beauville notes), one gets rho_{r,k} : Gamma_g = pi_1(M_g, X) -> PGL(H^0(SU_X(r), L^k)). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001))
The rank and level should be quantified as fixed integers r, k >= 1 in the setup of Theorem 7. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001))

The intended meaning of 'flat Hermitian metric' should be stated explicitly as projective unitarity of the projective connection / monodromy, exactly as Beauville writes in parentheses. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001))
refined_question: Let X be a smooth compact Riemann surface of genus g >= 2, let SU_X(r) be the moduli space of semistable rank-r vector bundles on X with trivial determinant, and let L be its determinant line bundle. For fixed integers r, k >= 1, Theorem 7 gives, as X varies over the moduli stack of smooth genus-g curves (informally M_g in the paper), a flat projective bundle with fibre P(H^0(SU_X(r), L^k)); equivalently, for a base curve X, a projective monodromy representation rho_{r,k} : Gamma_g = pi_1(M_g, X) -> PGL(H^0(SU_X(r), L^k)). Does there exist a flat Hermitian metric H_X on H^0(SU_X(r), L^k) making this projective connection projectively unitary, i.e. such that rho_{r,k}(Gamma_g) is contained in PU(H_X)? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently: is the projective connection of Theorem 7 on the bundle with fibres P(H^0(SU_X(r), L^k)) projectively unitary? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001))
justification: The draft is aimed at Beauville's Q8, not at any statement in §§1-8. Section 9 first defines the flat projective bundle for a family of smooth curves (Theorem 7), then the associated projective monodromy representation rho_{r,k} (Q7), and finally asks for a flat Hermitian metric whose existence is explicitly stated to be equivalent to rho_{r,k}(Gamma_g) being contained in PU(H_X) (Q8). Adding the definitions from §§1-2 and the moduli/monodromy setup from §9 makes the question fully stand-alone while staying exactly at the paper's scope. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001))
